title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost
abstract: arXiv:2611.13524v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to improve an agent using its own task experience. Its practical value depends on whether performance gains justify the full cost of self-improvement and task execution. We evaluate this trade-off on continual task streams, scoring each task before its feedback is used for subsequent updates. We define the \emph{RSI Tax} as the token cost of the self-improvement process and include it alongside task-execution costs in end-to-end evaluation. Across six methods and two language models, a bounded-note baseline matches or exceeds the observed accuracy of Meta-Harness, EvoSkill, and RRSI, with mean total-token savings of 65.6-71.0\%. We decompose the RSI Tax into verification, exploration, and writing costs, and track subsequent use of the associated state or artifact. translated_abstract: 递归自我改进（RSI）旨在利用智能体自身的任务经验来改进该智能体。其实际价值取决于性能提升是否能证明自我改进和任务执行的全部成本是合理的。我们在持续任务流上评估这种权衡，在每个任务的反馈被用于后续更新之前对其进行评分。我们将“RSI税”定义为自我改进过程的token成本，并将其与任务执行成本一起纳入端到端评估。在六种方法和两个语言模型的实验中，一个有界笔记基线在观察到的准确率上匹配或超过了Meta-Harness、EvoSkill和RRSI，平均总token节省达65.6-71.0%。我们将RSI税分解为验证、探索和写作成本，并追踪相关状态或产物的后续使用情况。对于这三种RSI方法，验证成本占RSI税总额的74.8-93.6%。RSI税的很大一部分也……
tldr: 本文提出“RSI税”概念以量化递归自我改进的token成本，发现有界笔记基线在准确率相当或更优的情况下可节省65.6-71.0%的总token开销，且验证成本占RSI税的74.8-93.6%，表明递归自我改进往往得不偿失。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "RSI Tax" to quantify the token cost of recursive self-improvement, showing that a simple bounded-note baseline matches or exceeds the accuracy of RSI methods while saving 65.6-71.0% of total tokens, with verification accounting for 74.8-93.6% of the tax—demonstrating that recursive self-improvement is often not worth its cost.
